critique.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_action: Missing a local activation-lead calibration of L=25 steps for the button near xy=(-0.163, -0.122) m. The retained motion supports P=160 and third passage T=200. At t=166, L=25 gives press-start S=175 and wait 9; the nominal L=20 fallback gives wait 14. The existing anchors do not specify this button neighborhood reliably.

The activation-lead calibration is missing for button center (-0.1623, -0.1220) m at this timing hover. Use L=25 steps here rather than the nominal 20-step fallback. The retained motion supports P=160, so the third passage is at step 200 and descent must start at step 175, now, rather than waiting five steps. Command [-0.1623, -0.1220, 0.0075, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper -1.

The retraction rule needed a localization cross-check for the partially occluded button after contact: use the center of the full circular button, not the center of its visible exposed patch, and check it against the retained unobstructed front image and current contact TCP. Here the button-centered retraction is approximately [-0.1662, -0.1551, 0.15], not [-0.149, -0.150, 0.15]. The descent/contact state already establishes that retraction with the gripper closed is appropriate; only the xy localization failed.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action:
Two action-rule corrections are needed; the motion_reference memory and its update rules remain sufficient and unchanged.

First, while hovering to stop the cube on its third target passage, the retained initial motion frames supported a full period of 160 steps and therefore a requested passage at step 200. For a button centered near (-0.1623, -0.1220) m, the policy used the nominal 20-step activation lead, waiting 14 steps at elapsed step 166 and another five steps at step 175, instead of waiting nine steps and then pressing. This is a SUFFICIENCY failure in the action calibration, not missing historical information or an unpredictable memory transition. Add button xy=(-0.1623, -0.1220) m to the existing L=25-step local calibration group for the specified timing-hover and press geometry. Select it using the localized button center, not the achieved hover TCP. It takes precedence over the nominal fallback and gives S=200-25=175. Retain the existing capped-wait and immediate-press tolerance rules; do not change the period inference or passage-count rules.

Second, after a successful descent and contact for a second-passage stop, the hand partially occluded the button. The retained motion_reference contained an unobstructed initial button view, and the current contact pose already established that retraction was appropriate. Nevertheless, the policy localized the exposed patch rather than the full circular button, retracting toward approximately (-0.149, -0.150) m instead of the button center near (-0.1662, -0.1551) m. This breaks waypoint SUFFICIENCY through an underspecified localization rule, not through inadequate memory. Extend the occlusion-recovery and retraction rules to cover partial occlusion explicitly: estimate the center of the full button circle from its boundary and white base, never the centroid of only its visible exposed portion. Cross-check this estimate against the retained unobstructed fixed-front reference, accounting for the raised button geometry, and against the current contact TCP as a consistency check. Do not triangulate features that correspond to different parts of the button in the two views. If current occlusion makes the center unreliable, recover the stationary button center from the retained unobstructed reference rather than shifting it to the exposed patch. Retract at that button-centered xy to z=0.15 with orientation [-3.1416, 0, 0] and gripper command -1. The contact TCP is only a cross-check, not a replacement for the button center. Preserve all other action rules.

fields.name: motion_reference
fields.description: With empty memory write [E0]. If the incoming list contains only E0 and this cycle shows that execution time has advanced, append all displayed execution front-camera labels in chronological order, excluding duplicates. Otherwise carry the incoming list unchanged. A zero-step action does not trigger appending. Once the initial motion frames have been appended, never append further frames or replace the list. Use the stored images and their absolute step labels as the reference for reconstructing the cube's periodic motion. e.g. ["E0", "E1", "E17", "E33", "E46"]
fields.annotation: An ordered list of execution keyframes documenting the initial cube motion. At the first cycle write [E0]. At the first cycle showing actual elapsed motion, append that cycle's displayed front-camera frame labels in chronological order, excluding duplicates. Freeze this list thereafter. These frames preserve the initial endpoint, early motion and its absolute timing, allowing the oscillation period and numbered future target passages to be inferred even when later images show the same positions again. They also retain the unobstructed button location. Do not select frames from future cycles. e.g. ["E0", "E1", "E17", "E33", "E46"]

texts.action:
Start by locating the gray circular button on its white base, the colored moving cube, and the purple target. Identify the center of the full gray circular button in the current front and wrist images, using its circular boundary and white base rather than the centroid of an exposed patch. Triangulate only corresponding features: do not pair different parts of the button in the two views. If either view does not support a reliable full-button center, use the occlusion-recovery rule below. Using each camera's intrinsics and world-to-camera extrinsics, construct world-space rays through that feature and estimate their closest intersection. Use the resulting point's xy as the button center, cross-checking against the white base. Account for the raised button top; do not intersect its center ray with the tabletop plane. Use this localized button-centered xy for approach, press and retraction. Do not use image left/right as robot left/right. When the TCP is initially high and has not approached the button, command [button_x, button_y, 0.15, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper command -1. Use the button center, not the slightly displaced achieved hover TCP, for subsequent commanded xy.

A TCP at approximately z=0.15 m and within about 0.02 m horizontally of the localized button center is already at the timing hover. In this region determine when to press using the timing rules below; do not insert another hover waypoint to refine xy or close visibly open fingers. Waits preserve the current gripper state. Keep gripper command -1 for the initial approach, press and retraction. Read the requested ordinal N from the goal. Use motion_reference together with the current motion frames and absolute elapsed_control_steps to reconstruct the cube's oscillation. The cube starts at one endpoint and moves smoothly back and forth; count a passage through the target in either direction, not a complete round trip. Fit the motion in world tabletop coordinates rather than assuming constant image velocity. In these trajectories the target is the midpoint of the oscillation: for full period P, passage times are P/4 + (N-1)P/2. Infer P from observed motion, not from the requested ordinal or the cube's color. The demonstrated periods include 120, 160 and 240 control steps. Initial and current frames should agree with the inferred phase; do not reset the passage count when the cube returns to an earlier-looking position.

Compute the requested passage time T_N = P/4 + (N-1)P/2 and press-start step S = T_N - L. L is the effective lead to button activation, not the full descent duration, and depends on button geometry rather than y alone. For a timing hover near z=0.15–0.156 m and a button-centered press command at z=0.0075 m, use these local spatial calibration anchors, grouped by effective activation lead: L=20 steps near button xy=(-0.200, -0.160) m or (-0.186, -0.174) m; L=22 near (-0.163, -0.007) m, and approximately 22 for the farther-right geometry near y=-0.19 m; L=23 near (-0.2150, -0.0354) m; L=24 near (-0.233, -0.013) m, (-0.2320, -0.1128) m or (-0.2236, -0.1452) m; L=25 near (-0.193, 0.095) m, (-0.1930, -0.0965) m, (-0.1775, -0.0937) m, (-0.1776, 0.0342) m, (-0.1867, 0.1497) m or (-0.1623, -0.1220) m. Select an applicable local calibration using the localized button center, not the achieved hover xy, cube color, requested ordinal or period. An applicable local calibration takes precedence over the nominal 20-step fallback. Away from these calibrated neighborhoods, 20 steps is only a nominal estimate; these anchors do not establish an exact lead formula for arbitrary locations. Do not substitute total descent duration for L.

Use the reported absolute elapsed_control_steps as t, not a sum of requested waits. If the hand is at the timing hover and t>=S-1, command [button_x, button_y, 0.0075, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper command -1 immediately. Otherwise, while hovering with t<S-1, wait min(30, round(S-t)) control steps in place, preserving the current gripper state. Do not take an extra full 30-step wait when fewer steps remain, or a needless one-step wait within the press-start tolerance. The press waypoint is intentionally below the contact-limited achieved TCP height; do not substitute the observed contact height for the command. Account for motion time: waiting until the cube visibly reaches the target before starting the descent is too late.

If the TCP is down at the button, approximately z=0.025 m, following a visible descent and contact, retract to [button_x, button_y, 0.15, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper command -1. Use the full-button center established by the localization and occlusion-recovery rules, not the exposed-patch centroid or the contact TCP xy. Do not press again simply because the cube remains near the target. A stopped cube after contact calls for retraction or, if already retracted, a short wait for termination.

If observations do not support a reliable period, compare retained initial motion with the current frames and wait a short interval, at most 10 steps, to disambiguate direction and speed rather than pressing on an uncertain passage. For partial or complete button occlusion, cross-check any full-circle center estimated from the visible boundary and white base against the retained unobstructed reference images, using the fixed front-camera calibration and the button's raised geometry rather than projecting its top onto the table. Never shift the stationary button center to the centroid of its visible exposed portion. If the current center estimate is unreliable, recover the center from the retained unobstructed reference. After contact, use the current contact TCP only as a consistency check, not as a replacement for the button center. Reserve a corrective button-centered hover for horizontal errors genuinely larger than the approximately 0.02 m timing-hover tolerance or an unsafe pose. An achieved hover offset within that tolerance does not require realignment; use the button center, not the achieved TCP xy, for the subsequent press. Never issue an identical-pose waypoint; use a wait when no movement is needed.
